主要内容: President Trump opposed funding mail-in voting, claiming $3.5 billion was insufficient for universal mail-in voting. Democrats, including Nancy Pelosi, accused him of undermining democracy by withholding election funding. Over 75% of U.S. voters were eligible to vote by mail in November. Postmaster General Louis DeJoy, appointed by Trump, implemented cost-cutting measures, including reducing overtime and late trips for mail carriers. These changes led to mail delays, raising concerns about medication delivery during the pandemic. Over 80 House members urged DeJoy to reverse the changes, and a bipartisan letter called for an audit. DeJoy denied that his relationship with Trump influenced his decisions, while Trump praised his performance improvements for the Postal Service.
